documents.title: The London Baptist Confession of 1689 (Condensed)
documents.blurb: The Second London Baptist Confession (1689), faithfully condensed chapter by chapter — the great Reformed Baptist confession — with explanatory notes.

documents.title: The New Hampshire Confession (Condensed)
documents.blurb: The New Hampshire Confession of Faith (1833), faithfully condensed article by article — the confession behind most American Baptist church covenants.

documents.title: The Augsburg Confession (Condensed)
documents.blurb: The chief articles of faith from the Augsburg Confession of 1530, faithfully condensed — the founding confession of the Lutheran Reformation, with notes.

documents.title: The Heidelberg Catechism, Lord's Day 1
documents.blurb: The full text of Lord's Day 1 of the Heidelberg Catechism (1563) — 'What is thy only comfort in life and death?' — with notes on its history and design.

documents.title: The Thirty-Nine Articles (Condensed)
documents.blurb: The Thirty-Nine Articles of Religion (1571), the doctrinal charter of Anglicanism, faithfully condensed article by article, with notes on the disputed lines.

documents.title: The Westminster Shorter Catechism, Q. 1–10
documents.blurb: The full text of the first ten questions of the Westminster Shorter Catechism (1647), beginning with the chief end of man, with plain-language notes.

documents.title: The Apostles' Creed
documents.blurb: The full text of the Apostles' Creed with plain-language notes on its history, the baptismal questions behind it, and what every loaded phrase is doing.

documents.title: The Athanasian Creed
documents.blurb: The full text of the Athanasian Creed (Quicunque Vult), the early church's most exacting statement of the Trinity and the incarnation, with plain notes.

documents.title: The Chalcedonian Definition
documents.blurb: The full text of the Definition of Chalcedon (AD 451) — one Christ in two natures, without confusion or division — with notes on Nestorius and Eutyches.

documents.title: The Nicene Creed
documents.blurb: The full text of the Nicene Creed of AD 381, with notes on Arius, homoousios, the filioque dispute between East and West, and why one Greek word mattered.
